title: AI Museum Dataset
tagline: Web-based visualization/landing page for my AI Museum Dataset independent study in Fall 2025

problem.blurb: Optimize and visualize a multimodal AI dataset for collaborative use and study design
problem.paragraph: This site is a visualization of 56-item dataset of artifact descriptions used in a design research study. When created, the dataset was not intended for research use and upon joining MultiSense.Studio and working under Dr. Stangl, I identified a need to better visualize and centralize the dataset so it could be referenced during the study and shared among my colleagues in the lab.

overview.summary: This is a web visualization of a multimodal cultural heritage dataset to support research activities in the field of multimodal AI and cultural heritage.
goals: a multimodal dataset, including text and images
study design and inquiry for design research endeavors
results: A publicly-accessible HTML site backed by JSON data that displays the multimodal dataset as a table for reference and distribution in research contexts.

background: I created this dataset during my time as an accessibility intern at the Robert C. Williams Museum of Papermaking in summer 2025. Through an iterative process, I collected images of museum artifacts and accompanying label text, consulted museum and accessibility experts to develop skills in authoring alt text for museums, and prompted a large language model to generate descriptive text designed to function as both interpretive description and alt text for accessibility.

This dataset will be used primarily in a design research study investigating how to design and evaluate documentation methods that promote critical reflection among museum professionals as they engage with AI-driven interpretive and accessibility systems. By framing dataset documentation as both a methodological and pedagogical practice, this study situates AI systems as collaborators in interpretive and ethical reflection and proposes alternative text as context documentation that reflects the interpretive, ethical, and communicative decisions embedded in multimodal museum data.
citations: Datasheets for Digital Cultural Heritage Datasets
Research on the Application of Artificial Intelligence to Accessibility Services in Science Museums

methods.title: Structuring the Dataset for Usability
methods.summary: The dataset as created in the internship was stored as a PowerPoint presentation for internal use at the museum, but JSON offered a scaleable, structured, readable format that optimized the dataset for research contexts.
methods.description: The dataset's initial PowerPoint format was effective in museum contexts for succinctly visualizing the artifact and its accompanying description, but the inquiry of this study required underlying metadata to better consider authorship, provenance, decision-making, and process. Incorporating this granularity in slide format would render the dataset illegible and difficult to navigate for researchers, as well as created a file far too large for the frequent and iterative LLM usage in the study. JSON mitigated these issues by structuring the data in an array of objects with key-value pairs for each metadata attribute. This consistent, machine-readable, and compact file more explicity paired artifacts and label copy with their accompanying descriptions and preserved the content of the original dataset while optimizing it for human use and LLM co-design for varying research contexts.
media: A sample of the dataset as delivered at the end of the internship. This PowerPoint contained an additional 50 human-authored descriptions that were not included in the study and therefore not translated to JSON
Structuring the dataset as a JSON array allowed for multi-platform use, enhanced readbility, and prepared the dataset for use in digital contexts

methods.title: Balancing Completeness and Readability in a Multimodal Dataset
methods.summary: Using Fetch API and JavaScript, the JSON data was rendered as a static HTML Table and hosted with GitHub Pages. The data is intended to be examined as a complete corpus, meaning the web visualization prioritized completeness and readability over interaction design.
methods.description: Because the dataset needed to be viewed in full, the visualization did not offer a querying or search function for navigation. This prevented filtering or selective viewing of data, maintaining the operational integrity originally preserved by converting the PowerPoint to a JSON array. Similarly, the page has no CSS styling to avoid detracting focus from the visual elements of the dataset or jeopardizing the legibility of the textual elements. These decisions, though contradictory to conventional design principles, optimized this visualization for the desired research contexts and encourage the careful review and critical consideration being explored in the independent study.

findings: Centralized dataset and facilitated access, sharing, and reuse among lab members
Introduced extended functionality by serving as a landing page for the independent study project
Supported dataset evaluation, analysis, and study design by enabling external access to dataset
Established a reusable model for lightweight web-based visualization of multimodal research datasets

reflection.paragraph: This site enabled remote sharing and access to the dataset during the study design and execution process, and using JSON allows for modularity and adaptability as new insights on AI-generated museum content arise throughout this study and future work. One major limitation of the site is the lack of querying and interactivity, as it is a static table of the dataset and its composite parts. This was a deliberate choice: the dataset was intended to be viewed as a complete corpus and applied to areas like model training and ethical evaluations, meaning preserving its integrity was prioritized over the usability benefits of a querying mechanism.
reflection.futureWork: This dataset was foundational to my independent study and connected to several other studies conducted by my fellow lab members. This simple, accessible visualization facilitated use and distribution of the dataset, suggesting that similar implementations for other experimental datasets would be an effective and necessary choice. Moreover, the decision to use this site as a central page for the independent study by including my abstract and linking to the publication enhances its functionality beyond data visualization to a scientific communication tool. These two uses could likely be replicated in future projects that center specific datasets.

title: Born in the Anthropocene
tagline: An interactive narrative exploring a sustainable future based in collective welfare and critical thought

problem.blurb: Before we can work toward more positive futures, we have to imagine them. Work in a team to imagine a more sustainable future society.
problem.paragraph: Despite the promising and novel innovations enabled by the advent of artificial intelligence (AI), this development has also had immediate and severe environmental impacts predicted to continue. In the face of rapidly changing climate and this new, ubiquitous environmental pressor, we must find and develop more sustainable structure for future generations

overview.summary: This is a design futuring project where fabulation was used to imagine, propose, and explore a sustainable future world with an interactive program.
goals: an interactive program exploring the proposed society
results: An interactive narrative and integrated p5.js sketch allowing users to explore our proposed future

background: During this course, sustainability was discussed under the lens of the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). These 17 goals are integral to the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, and call all countries of the world into partnership to address systemic deprivations like hunger and poverty and improve health, safety, education and economic growth while also addressing direct climate change and conservation concerns. In proposing a sustainable future society, we turned to the SDGs to determine how we could amplify one of these dimensions.

Our speculative narrative explored sociocultural aspects of sustainability, addressing poverty, hunger, education, and sustainable communities (SDGs 1,2,4, and 11, respectively). We hope to suggest that by focusing on creativity, critical thought, community values, and collective welfare, we could raise generations of more ethical, sustainably minded individuals. To do this, we devised a society with free healthcare, subsidized housing, universal basic income, and most importantly, a postmodern education that encouraged skepticism, curisoity, and creativity from early education.
citations: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs

methods.title: Brainstorming
methods.summary: We began with a 40 minute brainstorming session where we suggested different issues, societal structures, or narratives we might explore.
methods.description: Our goal was to have at least 50 unique ideas by the end of the session to sort into clusters and direct our design process. Our ideas initially focused on speculating the future of AI and its environmental impacts, but we soon expanded to more sociocultural ideas involving future relationships, power structures, economies, political systems, and more. By the end of the session we had 5 clusters of ideas: AI/LLMs, Conciousness, Infrastructure, Culture and Society, and Public Health
media: We settled on exploring culture and society since that's where we had the most ideas and common ground

methods.title: Proposed Concept
methods.summary: We settled on exploring sociocultural aspects of our sustainable future, focusing particularly on education and community. Our initial idea for the interactive program was a city builder game developed in p5.js
methods.description: We found that many of our ideas imagined novel educational systems that differed from our current education model in structure, length, content, delivery, or some combination of the four. From there, we consulted our background research on postmodern education to extrapolate the social structures and political and economic systems of our proposed society.
media: In the presentation, we emphasized our society as 'people first', noting how an emphasis on critical and creative thought would create a more connected, empathetic society

methods.title: Version 1
methods.summary: We submitted a functional prototype of the grid system for our city builder game, and received feedback from classmates, TAs, and community stakeholders based on our proposal and prototype.
methods.description: The critical feedback we received on version 1 was that our city builder concept did not adequately explore the robust sociocultural, educational, or economic dynamics we had proposed. Instead, it was suggested that an interactive narrative would better situated for exploration of these ideas.
media: Though we did not keep the city builder concept as a standalone product, we were still able to further develop and incorporate this prototype into the final narrative.

methods.title: Creating the Interactive Narrative
methods.summary: Based on feedback from version 1, we re-evaluated our proposal and decided an interactive narrative would be better fit for exploring our proposed society.
methods.description: We outlined a short, 3-part narrative and corresponding decision tree, where users would play through childhood, young adulthood, and old age as members of our proposed society. Upon the start of the game, players are assigned a sustainability score of 10 and as they navigate the narrative, different decisions increase or decrease that score. This score is revealed at our checkpoints, where we were able to still incoporate the initial p5.js sketch.
media: After writing the outline and decision tree in a Word document, we translated our story to Twine
We decided to embed the city builder sketch as a checkpoint between the three parts of the narrative

findings: Strong introduction to design futuring and speculative design with digital media
Developed a new research interest/application in using interactive narratives for design futuring
Allowed exposure to and familiarity with Twine for prototyping
Improved collaborative communication, organization, and task delegation skills

reflection.paragraph: This project was a valuable opportunity to improve my understanding of Twine as a prototyping/development tool for hypertext narratives. I successfully translated a traditional narrative into hypertext, considering the branches of the narrative and how different choices allowed for the exploration of key themes in our proposed future.
reflection.futureWork: As my first foray into design futuring, it was fascinating to see how I may use interactive narratives as sites for speculative fiction. With more time, I would've liked to better establish the world of our proposed future, creating a cohesive and solid background upon which to explore the social and cultural determinants of sustainability.
